stances.claim: This column is the third in a series on PNoy's Sona-cited daang matuwid achievements -- following A375 (Maguindanao) and A374 (three-senator PDAF) -- and continues the analytical theme that none of these cases will be resolved within PNoy's term
The Aug 11 SC Resolution granted Enrile's bill-of-particulars petition but denied his prayer to annul his arrest and detention; the more crucial bail petition is poised for ruling soon

GMA's electoral sabotage case in RTC Pasay led to bail-granted June 12, 2012 because the prosecution's evidence -- only a lone witness -- was not credible and failed to establish the 'strong' evidence required; the CA agreed and dismissed the prosecution's appeal

On April 6, 2015, the SBN Special Division of five denied GMA's demurrer 3-2 -- majority (Dela Cruz, Inoturan, Lagos as ponente) found a prima facie case of plunder; minority (Ponferrada and Quiroz) opined the elements of plunder were not proven and the charges should be downgraded to malversation, which would entitle GMA and Aguas to bail

Coaccused differential is stark: Morato, Roquero, Taruc, and Villar had their demurrers granted and were acquitted; Valencia was downgraded to malversation with P500,000 bail; only GMA and former PCSO executive Aguas remain without bail

GMA's April 8 motion to transfer detention to her La Vista home rests on her self-description as '68 years old, has undergone three spinal surgeries, remains frail and thin' and not a flight risk -- invoking the presumption of innocence and the prospect of better recovery

Two precedents support GMA's house-arrest motion: Estrada was transferred to his Tanay farm during his plunder detention under GMA's own presidency; Salonga was placed 'under house arrest in the custody of Mrs. Lydia Salonga' during the Marcos regime -- both demonstrate the SBN's institutional flexibility on house arrest

Like the other PNoy-Sona-cited achievements, GMA's cases will not be decided within PNoy's term ending June 30, 2016 -- and CJ promises to answer what happens after he relinquishes the presidency in next Sunday's column

one_paragraph_summary: Panganiban writes the third installment of his series on PNoy's daang matuwid Sona-cited achievements, following his prior columns on the Maguindanao massacre trial (A375) and the PDAF cases of three senators (A374). On a specific point from the prior column, he notes that on August 11 the Supreme Court released a Resolution granting Senator Enrile's petition for a bill of particulars but denied his prayer to annul his arrest and detention -- the more crucial bail petition is still pending. This column takes up the third set of Sona-cited cases: those involving former President Gloria Macapagal-Arroyo. Two cases have been filed against her. The first charged her with electoral sabotage for her alleged role in the 2007 Maguindanao election manipulation; her coaccused include former Maguindanao governor Andal Ampatuan Sr. (recently passed away) and Lintang Bedol, the former provincial Comelec supervisor of Maguindanao. Because she was indicted with a capital offense, she was arrested by the Regional Trial Court of Pasay, but on June 12, 2012, the RTC granted her bail on the ground that the prosecution's evidence -- the testimony of a lone witness -- was not strong; the Court of Appeals dismissed the prosecution's appeal. However, she was not released because of the second case: plunder before the Sandiganbayan First Division for the alleged unauthorized disbursement of P366 million in PCSO funds. After the prosecution rested, GMA and her coaccused filed a demurrer. Because the three members of the First Division were divided, a Special Division of five was created per the SBN Internal Rules. On April 6, 2015, a majority of three (Justices Efren Dela Cruz, Napoleon Inoturan, and Rafael Lagos as ponente) denied the demurrer, holding a prima facie case of plunder; unless GMA and her remaining coaccused (former PCSO executive Benigno Aguas) present countervailing evidence, they would be convicted. The minority of two (Justices Rodolfo Ponferrada and Alex Quiroz) opined that the elements of plunder were not proven; charges should be downgraded to malversation, entitling GMA and Aguas to bail. The coaccused outcomes are stark: former PCSO chair Manuel Morato, former board members Raymundo Roquero and Jose Taruc, and former COA chair Reynaldo Villar were all acquitted; former PCSO chair Sergio Valencia was downgraded to malversation with P500,000 bail. Frustrated, GMA filed on April 8, 2015 a motion to transfer her detention from the Veterans Memorial Medical Center to her house at 14 Badjao Street, La Vista, Quezon City, averring she is not a flight risk because she is '68 years old, has undergone three spinal surgeries, remains frail and thin, and to this day enjoys the presumption of innocence... [and] hopes that [her] house arrest can help her recuperate and heal more quickly and fully.' Two precedents support the motion: former President Estrada was allowed to be transferred to his Tanay, Rizal farm during his plunder detention under GMA's own presidency, and during the Marcos regime opposition Senator Jovito Salonga was placed 'under house arrest in the custody of Mrs. Lydia Salonga.' Despite the SBN's MR being pending, hearing on GMA's countervailing evidence is scheduled for August 26. Like the other Sona-cited achievements, GMA's cases will not be decided within PNoy's term ending June 30, 2016 -- CJ promises to answer what happens after he relinquishes the presidency next Sunday.
